facts.label: Financial interpretation and source conflicts
facts.text: Cash fell from September 6,261 to December 2,459. The complete reported bridge is OCF +752, investing −24, financing −4,516 and FX −14, net change −3,802. Financing includes dividend/equivalent cash payments −4,396, repurchases −316, securitization cash proceeds +163, option proceeds +35 and financing costs/other −2; the remaining source debt-flow cells display dashes. The annual handoff's known October 4,348 payment is not the whole quarterly distribution line: the quarter reports 4,396. spans.text: # CP-0 — TDG retained interim source readiness
## Request
Prepare the four retained HTML filings for financial analysis, prioritizing the
December 28, 2024 Form 10-Q and its comparative columns. Execution is the current
host model with local tools and existing preparation code, with conversation
context available. No provider/API or imported readiness runtime was invoked.
The supplied pack is historical and does not establish current 2026 conditions.
Result: **ready with limitations for the next CP-1 increment**. The primary
statements, cash/debt notes and period metadata can be read. Full content/visual
coverage of all four filings and full module-workbook sufficiency remain open.
## Sources
`source-preparation/manifest.json` pins all four raw sources, extracted text and
inline metadata. All twelve raw/text/metadata hashes matched on this run. The
raw HTML files are issuer evidence; generated text and inline JSON are reading
aids. Paths below are relative to the project root under
`data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/`; corresponding `.txt`/`.xbrl.json` aids are in this
run's `source-preparation/` directory.
| Source | Raw filename | Raw SHA-256 |
Method: Deploy V-derived source readiness, amended for actual source coverage
and the current Markdown transport as in `METHODOLOGY-REVIEW.md`;
`src/deploy_vii/methods/cp0.md` records the later adaptation's pinned reference
`bd71346301b373afa72655916a4c1b42bf4c9823`. Exact current method/instruction
hashes are recorded in the verification record. The existing annual PDF is a
separate retained presentation of FY2024; H3 is not byte-identical to it.
## Findings
### Identity, authority, accounting and periods
All four covers identify **TransDigm Group Incorporated**, SEC file 001-32833,
and the inline contexts identify CIK 0001260221. Each cover says either Form
10-Q or Form 10-K and names the reporting date. These are retained filings;
external retrieval, authenticity and completeness against SEC exhibits were
not checked again. Filename dates were not used as the identity oracle.
H4 text line 197 defines the Company as TransDigm Group Incorporated and its
subsidiaries, identifies unaudited interim information, U.S. GAAP annual
accounts, the audited September comparison balance, normal recurring management
adjustments and prior-year reclassifications described as immaterial. It says
the interim results are not necessarily indicative of the full year. These
statements support consolidated interim analysis, not a new audit opinion.

| H1 | Cover line 4: “For the quarterly period ended March 30, 2024”; income heading lines 78 onward; cash flows lines 171 onward | Quarter 2023-12-31–2024-03-30; YTD 2023-10-01–2024-03-30; comparative quarter 2023-01-01–2023-04-01. |

organic growth, acquisition contribution or durable margins. H4's MD&A provides

maturity. It also explicitly attributes no first-quarter term-loan principal

## Calculations
`CP-1-attempt-1-calculations.json` retains 634 checks: statement and equity
identities, gross/cost/net debt reconciliation, segment/issuer EBITDA bridges,

scale/sign. Raw HTML table cells were read separately from the production inline

rows; no golden fixture or production financial calculation supplied them.
The original visible dashes remain in the handoff; transformed zero is not a
missing-data substitution. The unsupported number-word fact “three” describes
reportable segment count and remains outside numeric-reader support.
Checks do not establish source authenticity or comprehensive visual review.
The numeric checks and source table copy are deterministic local work; the
interpretation above is the current model's actual response to the instructions.
Neither establishes isolated API reliability or receipt-based runtime acceptance.

| G4 | Restricted/unrestricted cash, current borrowing conditions and forward cash-use plan absent | CP-2D/CP-2G need those inputs before sufficiency/runway; issuer cash liquidity remains attributed. |

| G5 | Full executed debt/guarantee/collateral documents and lender covenant certificate absent | CP-4/CP-3C cannot infer capacity, priority or covenant headroom from annual/interim narrative alone. |

| G6 | Adjustment quality, maintenance capex, acquisition pro formas and sustained cash conversion unproven | CP-1D/CP-2 must assess definitions/recurrence; calculated OCF-minus-capex is only a proxy. |
| G7 | Original-source external-version and visual limitations from CP-0 persist | Use exact locators for consequential claims; obtain specific missing evidence rather than invent it. |

spans.text: # CP-1B — TDG actual first-quarter earnings update
## Request
Compare the issuer's first fiscal-quarter results, preserving exact periods:
current October 1–December 28, 2024 (89 inclusive days), prior October 1–December
30, 2023 (91 inclusive days). Both are labelled thirteen weeks by the issuer.
These are reported fiscal-quarter comparisons with a calendar-length limitation;
no dates, annualization or daily-rate adjustments are invented.
**Earnings view, Analyst Interpretation, Medium confidence:** reported sales,
operating income and operating cash increased, while distributions/repurchases
reduced the cash buffer. That supports historical earnings improvement with a
material cash-allocation constraint. It does not establish current liquidity
sufficiency, sustainable FCF, a rating or future refinancing ability.
## Sources
Actually opened and consumed `CP-1-attempt-2.md`, SHA-256
`8be815a5103120678d923721a7c52ab3ebaad28985a98df1f673be092d227582`, and the CP-0 source map.
This supplies all primary-statement, signed EBITDA bridge, account and period
facts below. Targeted checking uses H4, the retained December 28, 2024 10-Q,
SHA-256 `9bdfd29ebc3c57b72d506e7dff2a2ca2e3179035deb4941dcd026523a5b8595a`.
Locators are zero-based HTML table/row coordinates or one-based text-aid lines
identified by the source-preparation manifest. Evidence is unaudited consolidated
U.S. GAAP filing information, with management's non-GAAP measures attributed.
Selected broader method and later calculation/owner candidates:
- `skills/cp-1b-earnings-delta/references/REF_CP-1B_STEPS.md`: `5a5baa859471254ecba1807dfd067a8cc648fb5e0d40907dbc45a9b1edbd4889`.
- `src/deploy_workflow/earnings.py`: `6ae089ec784d105507b3577bddf517c787312c96da570640541d65baf4c0d8ed`.
- `src/deploy_workflow/owners/cp1b.py`: `db6d9307bb2f39abab7809a1a1660db0a9b2ec01a3523936d912500dd78b982d`.
- `src/deploy_vii/model/_cells.py`: `38c2ec4493b9b53065361db748a596687c7381eaf91659bc48fd9707ce7f2549`.
- `runs/tdg-003/CP-1B-instructions.md`: `412c3dd383807f50d811839c10613b984bd7c889dcd1fbedd0bff5dbaf056c0f`.
Execution is current-host-model analysis with local tools and existing Decimal
arithmetic, not isolated provider/API execution or legacy owner acceptance.
Actual private validation/label-function refusals are retained in the calculation
record. No IFRS identity, accepted execution head or provider receipt was fabricated.
## Findings
### Definition lock and top sheet
Amounts are USD millions except reported percentages. Ordinary EBITDA is the
issuer's net-income + D&A + net-interest + tax bridge; EBITDA As Defined adds
its signed adjustments. The source-rounded EBITDA margin below is explicitly
**As Defined**, not ordinary EBITDA margin. OCF-minus-capex 710/600 is a simple
cash-after-capex proxy, not a newly adopted FCF definition. Missing issuer FCF,
discretionary cash flow and maintenance/growth capex remain unavailable.
Reported current cash is 2,459. The issuer's cash-liquidity measure is 3,308,
including disclosed revolver availability 849; unrestricted/access conditions
remain unresolved. Carrying debt 25,049 and mechanical net carrying debt 22,590
are December instants. Their September comparisons 24,880 and 18,619 are
sequential balance changes, not prior-year December leverage observations.
No annual/LTM leverage, senior-secured leverage, covenant cover or FFO/debt is
calculated from this single-quarter update.
### Financial performance / comparator register
Comparison basis: reported fiscal Q1 year over year; exact window limitation
above applies to every row. Source locations are CP-1's named statement/bridge
sections and original H4 tables 10, 14 and 66. Percent changes below are calculated
from CP-1 values, rounded to two decimals only for display. Capex is kept signed;
positive percentage change means a larger outflow magnitude.
<!-- table-id: cp1b.model_comparator_register -->
| Metric | Prior | Current | Absolute change | Change % | Definition / source |
| Revenue | 1789 | 2006 | 217 | 12.13% | Reported sales |
| COGS | 747 | 771 | 24 | 3.21% | Reported expense |
| Gross profit | 1042 | 1235 | 193 | 18.52% | Reported |
| SG&A | 220 | 211 | -9 | -4.09% | Reported expense |
| Intangible amortization | 35 | 50 | 15 | 42.86% | Not total D&A |
| EBITDA | 859 | 1087 | 228 | 26.54% | Issuer ordinary EBITDA |
| EBITDA As Defined | 912 | 1061 | 149 | 16.34% | Signed issuer adjustments |
| EBIT | 787 | 974 | 187 | 23.76% | Reported operating income |
| Net interest expense | 300 | 378 | 78 | 26.00% | Accrual expense, not cash paid |
| Cash interest paid | 205 | 162 | -43 | -20.98% | Already included in OCF |
| Cash taxes paid | 11 | 37 | 26 | 236.36% | Net of refunds; already in OCF |
| Capex signed cash flow | -36 | -42 | -6 | 16.67% | Maintenance/growth split absent |
| OCF minus capex proxy | 600 | 710 | 110 | 18.33% | Calculated; not issuer FCF |
| Net income | 382 | 493 | 111 | 29.06% | Reported |
| Closing cash | 4135 | 2459 | -1676 | -40.53% | Quarter-end instants; not unrestricted cash |
| Additional required measure | Result / limitation |
| D&A | 71 prior / 90 current; source bridge, not just intangible amortization. |
| Gross margin | Source-rounded 58.2% → 61.6%; +3.4 percentage points. |
| EBITDA As Defined margin | Source-rounded 51.0% → 52.9%; +1.9 percentage points. |
| Maintenance/growth capex, aggregate normalized WC, issuer FCF and DCF | Not established under CP-1's definitions; do not invent a split or new metric. |

| Debt/EBITDA, net debt/EBITDA, senior-secured leverage, cash-interest cover and (EBITDA−capex)/cash-interest cover | No comparable reported/covenant ratios or accepted matching LTM bases in this increment. Quarterly quotients would answer a different question. |
| FFO/debt, issuer-FCF/debt and issuer-FCF conversion | Not Calculable: missing defined FFO/FCF and applicable matched bases. The cash-after-capex proxy does not substitute. |
### Variance mechanics and comparative credit evaluation
Revenue increased 217. The issuer's organic/acquisition sales categories explain
that arithmetic as organic +118 and acquisition +99 (H4 table 51). These are
management classifications. They do not independently isolate price, volume,
mix or purchase-accounting effects. Source MD&A attributes cost performance in
part to operating strategy and fixed overhead spread over volume, and identifies
FX gains (text 540); those are management explanations, not a causal model
validated by the comparative totals.
Ordinary EBITDA increased 228 while As Defined increased 149. The signed
adjustment bridge explains the difference: current 13 + 25 − 64 = −26 versus
prior 2 + 51 + source dash = 53, a decrease of 79. Thus growth in the adjusted
measure is lower than ordinary EBITDA growth. Recurrence/acceptance belongs in
CP-1D, especially the negative Other row and acquisition-related costs.
OCF increased 116, and the inherited cash-after-capex proxy increased 110.
Cash interest paid fell 43 while interest expense rose 78. The accrued-interest
change in CP-1's cash-flow statement is relevant to timing; these quantities
cannot be interchanged or subtracted again from OCF. Positive reported earnings
and OCF are the strongest counterargument to interpreting lower cash as an
operating collapse.
The cash buffer nevertheless fell: December cash is 1,676 below the prior-year
December balance and 3,802 below September. The sequential cash decline is
reconciled by the actual OCF/investing/financing/FX bridge, including financing
outflow 4,516. This indicates cash-allocation pressure alongside improved
historical earnings. No claim of covenant breach or impending distress follows.
No accepted budget, management numerical guidance, agency case or prior forecast
benchmark was supplied. Actual-versus-guidance/agency evaluation is unavailable.
Sequential earnings and LTM comparison also remain unavailable from this checked
increment; do not treat the static CP-2A shocks as forecasts of this quarter.
### Corporate actions, comparability and conflicts
| Event / scope | Evidence and comparison effect | Credit consequence / limitation |

| FY2024 acquisitions contribute to both comparison definitions | CP-1/H4 table 51 acquisition sales 112/13; earlier acquisitions and measurement-period adjustments appear in Note 2 | Organic categories help identify contribution, but no complete acquisition-adjusted like-for-like/pro-forma bridge is established. |

| CPI and SEI settlement updates | H4 text 215/234: CPI cumulative cash price 1,386 includes 1 paid in fiscal Q1; SEI 171 includes 1 paid in Q1 | Annual CPI 1,385 and interim 1,386 retain their dates/settlement distinction; no silent overwrite of prior canonical value. |

| October 18, 2024 distribution | H4 text 587: common dividend 4,216 and vested equivalents 131; annual handoff/PDF 146 identifies equivalents 132 | **Unresolved disclosure difference:** 131 versus 132. Retain both; do not force equality, classify the difference as rounding, or derive an unsupported residual allocation. |
| Whole-quarter distributions | CP-1 cash flows: 4,396 paid in the quarter, versus 2,038 prior | Different scope from the single October event; not a conflict requiring those totals to match. |

| Share repurchases | CP-1/current equity and H4 text 274: 252,800 shares for 316; remaining authorization 972 | Cash allocation competes with creditor buffers; authorization is not a cash commitment or legal-capacity opinion. |

| Securitization draw | CP-1 debt/flow maps: rounded quarterly cash proceeds 163 and carrying debt 649; annual event disclosure 162.5 | Preserve reporting precision, period and principal/carrying distinction; do not count the same financing twice. |

| Business-sale/FX and other adjustment items | CP-1 EBITDA footnote definitions and cash-flow gain row | Affect comparability; no unsupported sale date, buyer or allocation of the entire Other row is inferred. |

| Period/accounting compatibility | Real dates differ in length; both source periods remain U.S. GAAP | No annualization or IFRS relabeling. Literal fiscal-quarter differences can be shown with the stated limitation. |
### Validation, add-backs and publication readiness
<!-- table-id: cp1b.model_validation_register -->
| Metric / period | CP-1 versus original source | Result |
| Revenue 2006/1789; ordinary EBITDA 1087/859; As Defined 1061/912 | H4 tables 10/66, literal values and definitions | PASS for retained values; no replacement canonical figures. |
| CFO 752/636 and quarter closing cash 2459/4135 | H4 table 14 and independent statement checks | PASS; prior cash is the actual comparative December instant. |

| December carrying debt 25049 and cash-after-capex proxy 710/600 | CP-1 classification/proxy formulas, not issuer-reported totals under those exact names | PASS for stated derived meanings; no prior-year debt inferred. |
| Issuer FCF / reported leverage / guidance / workbook outputs | Not supplied or not published | WARN / unavailable; not zero and not a fabricated comparison. |
<!-- table-id: cp1b.addback_validation_register -->
| Issuer adjustment | Current / prior source cells | Label/definition match | Result |
| Acquisition transaction and integration-related expenses | 13 / 2 | Exact CP-1/H4 table 66 row 10 labels and source footnote | PASS transcription; not creditor acceptance. |
| Non-cash stock and deferred compensation expense | 25 / 51 | Exact CP-1/H4 table 66 row 11 labels | PASS transcription; not an assumption of cost disappearance. |
| Other, net | (64) / — | Exact CP-1/H4 table 66 row 12 and signed source footnote | PASS transcription; negative adjustment and source dash preserved. |
<!-- table-id: cp1b.cp_model_snapshot_fields -->
| field_id | value | status | source_id / locator | as_of |

| historical_performance | Reported fiscal Q1 sales, operating income and OCF increased; distributions and repurchases reduced the cash buffer. Adjusted and ordinary EBITDA growth differ because signed adjustments changed. | READY for this bounded historical field | H4 tables 10,14,66; CP-1 period/definition map | 2024-12-28 |
<!-- table-id: cp1b.model_readiness -->
| downstream_module | status | blocking evidence / explanation |

| CP-MODEL / delivery | historical field available; full publication remains restricted | No published workbook/chart validation, accepted LTM/current-accessibility/forward case, or resolution of 131/132 equivalents discrepancy. Preserve source scope and all limitations. |
### Monitoring and method changes justified by observed output
Track dated cash after distributions; future dividend/repurchase decisions;
revolver availability and borrowing conditions; the securitization renewal
milestone; operating cash versus interest accruals; adjusted-EBITDA definitions;
and organic/acquisition attribution. Evidence of sustained cash conversion,
accessible liquidity and policy restraint would strengthen the creditor case.
New extraction, weak conversion, restricted access or refinancing delays would
weaken it. Quantified covenant/rating thresholds remain absent.
The later pure period validator actually returned `incompatible_dimensions`
for the source-derived U.S. GAAP metadata. Its implementation hard-codes IFRS.
A separately supplied diagnostic report of actual nonzero deltas produced
`unsupported_pair` in its label function, which admits only flat or missing
comparisons. The source dates also fail its equal-calendar-duration condition;
that condition was inspected without falsifying the accounting metadata to
reach it. These are limitations of the imported earnings slice, not model
inability or issuer failures. Before automation, it needs matched actual
accounting/perimeter handling, a disclosed fiscal-comparability policy and
ordinary nonzero/driver/guidance assessments. No synthetic label substitution
or global accounting/date relaxation is justified.
## Calculations
`CP-1B-attempt-1-calculations.json` retains the exact consumed handoff hash,
source dates, 17 numerical comparisons, two margin-point changes and actual
legacy diagnostic results. Existing `_cells.CONTEXT` supplies 38-digit half-even
Decimal arithmetic; independent Fraction checks verify each delta exactly and
growth within 1e-35. Display is rounded only after those checks. The additional
signed-adjustment and sales-bridge arithmetic is retained in the same record.
## Gaps
All CP-1 G1–G7 remain. Additional constraints: the 131/132 vested-equivalents
source difference needs clarification; complete corporate-action/perimeter,
acquisition-adjusted and normalized recurring performance remain unproven;
quarterly leverage/covenant bases, peer/agency/guidance benchmarks, full LTM
series and workbook outputs are not available. The broader method's validation
registers do not prove that publication ran. Stronger confidence and current
liquidity/refinancing conclusions require those specific inputs.
## Next module
**CP-2D** should use the actual reported cash bridge and distinguish the October
event from whole-quarter distributions, retaining the equivalents discrepancy.
**CP-1D** should challenge the actual signed adjustments and cash-conversion
interpretation, retaining missing recurrence evidence. **Delivery** can consume
the historical-performance field and checked comparison table now. CP-MEMO has
been replaced by actual deliverables; no extra memo analysis is required.
This earnings answer is source-limited host-model evidence; actual downstream
consumption remains required and the imported owner/runtime remains unqualified.

spans.text: # CP-1D — TDG earnings quality and absorbed adjusted-debt review
## Request
Challenge the actual issuer EBITDA bridge and identify debt-like obligations,
including CP-1E's absorbed responsibilities. Financial comparisons use FY2024
(2023-10-01–2024-09-30) and September 30, 2024 balances. The December quarter
and its comparator are separate recurrence evidence; they are not annual/LTM
denominators. USD millions unless noted. Execution: actual current-host-model
analysis with local tools and conversation context; no provider or owner runtime.
**Earnings-quality view: Medium confidence, source-limited.** The adjustments
are supported as reported entries, but their disclosure does not establish that
all should be accepted as sustainable credit earnings. Stock/deferred compensation
recurs, acquisition/refinancing categories repeat, and Other contains different
gains/costs. The negative quarterly Other adjustment must remain negative.
Quality-adjusted EBITDA is unresolved; no invented haircut produces a point value.
**Adjusted-debt view:** the stated carrying-debt/operating-lease/gross-pension
convention gives a known-item subtotal of 24,961. This is not a complete adjusted-
debt, covenant-debt or cash-availability conclusion. The material declared
distribution remains a separate cash commitment, and unresolved claims remain gaps.
## Sources
Actually consumed the annual `../tdg-002/CP-1-attempt-2.md`, quarterly
`CP-1-attempt-2.md`, actual `CP-1B-attempt-1.md` and CP-0 source map. Exact hashes
and selected source revisions are retained in `CP-1D-attempt-1-calculations.json`.
CP-1 owns reported amounts; CP-1B's transcription checks are inherited rather
than replaced by new canonical numbers.
| Evidence ID | Original source / located content |
| A | FY2024 annual PDF SHA-256 dc6a8ea6249e4e919d190a4bbb459d9bf4eded005b7d5680ae911b32d44d44af; PDF 52–54 definitions and two issuer bridges, 141–142 segment/three-year bridge. |
| D | Same PDF 105/126–133: CP-1 carrying debt and principal/cost classification; securitization, finance leases and separate facility terms. |
| P | Same PDF 134–136 pension note. PDF 134 rendered and visually checked in source-preparation/pdf134-pension.png; U.S./non-U.S. columns, gross liabilities, assets and net amounts confirmed. |
| L | Same PDF 147–148: operating/finance lease liabilities and payments, inherited from CP-1. |
| Q | December 10-Q SHA-256 9bdfd29ebc3c57b72d506e7dff2a2ca2e3179035deb4941dcd026523a5b8595a; CP-1 source tables 66/69, text 639–641/661–664 and CP-1B validated signed adjustments. |
| C | CP-1/CP-1A distribution facts and CP-1B's actual 131/132 equivalents difference; declared, payable, single-event paid and full-quarter paid are distinct. |
Selected method: earnings-quality plus absorbed adjusted-debt analytical breadth
in `skills/cp-1d-earnings-quality/SKILL.md`, SHA-256
`9682b2da83fe7fd3288cae31fc5d1cf7f6d2daa3de2fac297637fe13d5e8e2ae`;
later adaptation `src/deploy_vii/methods/cp1d.md`, SHA-256
Pure sums/quotients from `owners/cp1d.py` are reused, retaining exact arithmetic
and missingness. Its additional-financing bridge is a different analytical object.
Descriptive T1D/T1E numbering below follows the broader selected method, not the
later runtime's changed table meanings. CP-1E resolves to this artifact's debt phase.
## Findings
### T1D.1 — inherited signed adjustment register
| ID / period | Issuer description | Amount | Category / management rationale | Evidence |

| A1 FY2024 | Acquisition transaction and integration-related expenses | 70 | Integration, relocation, transaction/valuation/due-diligence costs and inventory step-up amortization; not a homogeneous saving. | A PDF 53 footnote 1; CP-1 bridge. |
| A2 FY2024 | Non-cash stock and deferred compensation expense | 217 | Compensation under stock/deferred-compensation plans. | A PDF 53 footnote 2. |
| A3 FY2024 | Refinancing costs | 58 | Debt issuance, extinguishment, refinancing and amendments. | A PDF 53 footnote 3. |
| A4 FY2024 | Other, net | 15 | FX, payroll-withholding, pension/deferred-compensation and miscellaneous items; no component allocation accepted here. | A PDF 53 footnote 4. |

| Q1 current quarter | Acquisition transaction and integration-related expenses | 13 | Same disclosed broad category, source actions not a new run-rate saving claim. | Q table 66 row 10 / footnote 1. |
| Q2 current quarter | Non-cash stock and deferred compensation expense | 25 | Reported noncash category, not proof that economic compensation disappears. | Q table 66 row 11. |
| Q3 current quarter | Other, net | (64) | Signed negative adjustment; source footnote describes gains/costs. | Q table 66 row 12 / footnote 3. |
No quarterly refinancing row is invented. Ordinary versus adjusted annual/quarter
amounts remain those in CP-1; neither is relabelled as covenant EBITDA.
### T1D.2 — achievability and normalisation assessment
| ID | Evidence of action / realisation | Assessment and counterevidence | Accepted normalisation / limitation |

| A1 / Q1 | Completed acquisitions and booked expenses are documented; no quantified savings plan or realised run-rate bridge is supplied. | Historical expense recognition is supported. Some transaction-specific costs may end; broad repeated category does not prove that every component is non-recurring. | Unresolved component-level treatment; no fraction or saving invented. |

| A2 / Q2 | Recognised compensation and noncash source classification are documented. | Supported transcription; recurring economic compensation remains a cost to the business/owners. Noncash does not imply a non-recurring cost. | Challenged as a non-recurring normalisation; no blanket conversion into cash-generating capacity. |

| A3 | Actual debt issues/refinancings documented. | Historical action occurred. Individual transaction costs can end, but repeated funding activity requires a normalised financing-policy assessment. | Unresolved sustainable treatment; no assumed annual absence. |

| A4 / Q3 | Reported net row and footnote components exist; cash/noncash/recurring split is not quantified. | Heterogeneous category, including gains; removing all components as a positive cost add-back would be wrong. | Unresolved; preserve annual +15 and quarterly −64 independently. |
### T1D.3 — recurrence test
| Category | Named prior periods and current evidence | Verdict / creditor mechanism |

| Acquisition/integration | FY2022 18, FY2023 18, FY2024 70; quarter comparisons 2/13. | Aggregate category repeats. Continuing acquisition policy can make such spending part of sustained cash demand even when each deal is distinct. Component-level non-recurrence remains unproven. |
| Stock/deferred compensation | FY2022 184, FY2023 157, FY2024 217; quarter comparisons 51/25. | Recurring category; do not call the whole expense a one-off or equate exclusion with free cash. |

| Refinancing | FY2022 1, FY2023 56, FY2024 58. | Repeated transaction category. It is not proof of the exact cost of future refinancing, but contradicts an unqualified statement that funding costs never recur. |

| Other | FY2022 (13), FY2023 16, FY2024 15; quarter comparisons —/(64). | Sign and mix vary. Recurrence cannot be assigned uniformly to each component from an aggregate net row. Source dash remains a dash. |
### T1D.4 — issuer control bridge and unresolved quality bridge
| Step | Source adjustment | Cumulative issuer EBITDA | Quality treatment / cumulative quality value |
| Ordinary issuer EBITDA | 3,813 | 3,813 | Reference base, not independently certified sustainable earnings. |
| Acquisition/integration | 70 | 3,883 | Unresolved; quality cumulative value unavailable. |
| Stock/deferred compensation | 217 | 4,100 | Recurring-cost challenge; cannot turn other unresolved items into zero. |
| Refinancing | 58 | 4,158 | Unresolved sustainable funding-cost treatment. |
| Other | 15 | 4,173 | Unresolved heterogeneous net item. |
The source bridge reconciles; a quality-adjusted point does not follow. Quarterly
control independently reconciles 1,087 + 13 + 25 − 64 = 1,061. Unresolved means
neither accepted nor rejected by default. No supposed Supported EBITDA is made
by starting at the already-adjusted 4,173 and adding the same 360 again.
### T1D.5 — annual cash-conversion test
| Basis / FY2024 | EBITDA | OCF | Calculated OCF / EBITDA | Explanation and creditor consequence |
| Ordinary issuer EBITDA | 3,813 | 2,045 | 53.63% | Cash conversion is partial; OCF reflects interest, taxes, working capital and other source-bridged items. |
| Issuer EBITDA As Defined | 4,173 | 2,045 | 49.01% | Larger denominator lowers the mechanical quotient. The issuer's OCF-to-EBITDA bridge, not a generic add-back story, supplies the components. |
| Quality-adjusted EBITDA | Unresolved | 2,045 | Not Calculable | Missing resolved denominator; no zero replacement or invented haircut. |
This is an annual conversion comparison, not cash available for discretionary
use. Capex, acquisitions and distributions are separate after-OCF uses. Interest,
taxes and working capital are not deducted again from OCF.
### T1D.6 — annual-balance leverage sensitivity
| Calculated measure, September 30, 2024 | Ordinary EBITDA | Issuer As Defined | Quality-adjusted EBITDA | Meaning |
| Carrying debt 24,880 / annual EBITDA | 6.5250x | 5.9621x | Not Calculable | Definition sensitivity, not reported/covenant leverage. |
| Mechanical net carrying debt 18,619 / annual EBITDA | 4.8830x | 4.4618x | Not Calculable | Uses reported cash, not established unrestricted cash; known distributions matter. |
### T1D.7 — earnings-quality gaps
| Gap | Missing evidence | Affected conclusion / follow-up |
| Component-level normalisation | Cost detail, cash/noncash split, actual integration milestones and future recurrence support | Resolve A1/A3/A4 before publishing quality-adjusted EBITDA. |
| Compensation economics | Recurring cash/deferred settlement and dilution policy | Assess sustainable burden without assuming all noncash cost disappears. |

| Complete source and forward case | Supplemental note coverage, forecast, legal/covenant basis and current cash access | No full sustainable-earnings, current leverage or covenant-capacity conclusion. |
### T1E.1 — obligation inventory, annual balance basis
| Item | Reported amount / date | Category and disclosure quality | Evidence |
| Finance leases | 262 at 2024-09-30 | Already part of CP-1 debt-note carrying debt. | D/L, CP-1 lease/debt registers. |
| Operating leases | 62 at 2024-09-30 | Recognised lease liability outside the chosen funded-debt sum. | L PDF 148. |
| Securitization | Carrying 486; gross 487 | Already separately included in CP-1 24,880 debt classification. | D PDF 130–131. |

| Defined-benefit pensions | Gross recognised liabilities 19 = U.S. 3 + non-U.S. 16; separate non-U.S. asset 13; aggregate net deficit 6 | Visually checked pension note. Benefit obligations 180 and plan assets 174 are different gross quantities; do not add benefit obligations wholesale. | P PDF 134, current-year columns. |
| Government refundable advances | 17 | Already in debt-note carrying amount; conditional repayment, not a conventional note. | D CP-1 facility register. |

| Declared dividend payable | 4,216 at 2024-09-30 | Material shareholder cash commitment, separately identified from funded debt; equivalents require their own scope/amount. | C, CP-1 balance sheet and PDF 146. |

| Factoring / reverse factoring / supplier finance | No separately quantified additional obligation established in this review | Trade payables alone do not prove financing; not an assumed zero. | Targeted disclosure/document follow-up required. |

| Hybrids / preferred claims / earn-outs / puts / other quasi-debt | No complete quantified register established | No default multiple or guessed zero. | Acquisition/financing/contingency documents needed. |
| Guarantees / perimeter | Intragroup guarantees are not automatically extra consolidated principal | Full legal perimeter and external contingent claims not reviewed. | CP-4 required. |
### T1E.2 — debt-like treatment and convention

| Finance leases / securitization / advances | Increment 0 for these already-counted items | Inclusion in the reported carrying base is evidenced. Adding them again would double count; this zero is a known no-second-addition, not missing-data imputation. |

| Operating leases | Add 62 to the known subtotal | U.S. GAAP/ASC 842 lease presentation; add the recognised operating liability to the selected funded-debt base. It is already on the broader balance sheet, so this is a reclassification for analytical debt, not creation of a new accounting liability. No additional lease multiple. |

| Pensions | Add gross recognised liabilities 19; do not offset the separately reported 13 asset | Primary convention does not assume asset transferability between plans. Net consolidated deficit 6 is retained as a different measure. Expected FY2025 funding is stated not material (PDF 135), not zero; the liability is not an immediate contribution demand. |

| Declared distribution | Separate committed cash-use analysis; outside this stated funded-debt/lease/pension subtotal | It competes for cash and must not be ignored in net-debt/liquidity reasoning. Adding a payable and also deducting the same payment from cash would double count its impact. Legal/cash-equivalent scope needs resolution. |

| CP-1 carrying debt | 24,880 | 24,880 | Long-term + current + separate securitization. |

| Gross recognised pension liabilities | 19 | 24,961 | No offset of separate asset. |
| Already-counted finance leases/securitization/advances | 0 | 24,961 | No duplicate addition. |
| Other unresolved claims | Unquantified | Full total unavailable | Known subtotal is not a complete adjusted-debt conclusion. |

| Ordinary EBITDA 3,813 | 6.5250x | 6.5463x | +0.0212x | Numerator convention changes the comparison; completeness and earnings-quality limits remain. |
| Issuer As Defined 4,173 | 5.9621x | 5.9815x | +0.0194x | Quantified lease/pension additions are small relative to the funded base; that does not bound unquantified claims or distribution effects. |
| Quality-adjusted EBITDA | Not Calculable | Not Calculable | Not Calculable | No resolved denominator or complete numerator. |

| Item | This analysis | Agency / alternative treatment | Status and reason |

The issuer reports real historical earnings and positive OCF, with both EBITDA
bridges reconciling. That is the strongest counterweight to treating all
adjustments as fictitious. It does not prove that repeated expenses cease or
that an adjusted earnings measure pays interest, capex and distributions.

cash after obligations and distributions → greater refinancing/access dependence.

restraint would strengthen the creditor case; further extraction or unresolved
adjustment growth would weaken it. Monitor signed adjustment composition,
recurrence, cash settlements, declared/paid distributions, lease/pension funding
